title: prefill oscillation damper and decode latency stabilizer
author: Arjun Mehta
description: Motivation: In production traces we see short-lived oscillations where the prefill admission rate and downstream decode pacing fight each other: the scheduler briefly ramps up prefill windows to keep GPUs busy, which triggers KV-priming churn and increases per-token latency; the decode stage then throttles, causing the scheduler to overshoot again. This PR introduces a lightweight Prefill Oscillation Damper (POD) and a Decode Latency Stabilizer (DLS) that act as soft controllers between the admission scheduler, the kernel selector, and the KV priming policy to reduce these oscillations without sacrificing throughput. Key ideas: 1) a leaky integrator on prefill window size that penalizes rapid expansions when KV hitrate drops; 2) a deadline-aware kernel throttle that defers non-critical prefill kernels when decode latency headroom is low; 3) transient KV-priming hysteresis to avoid repeated warm/evict cycles for the same shard; 4) observability hooks and benchmarks to validate stability vs baseline. Implementation summary: - runtime/scheduler/pod_controller.{cc,h} implements a small PID-like controller (proportional+integral with exponential decay) that observes per-queue decode latency p50/p95 and KV-hit-rate, and outputs a damped multiplier for prefill window requests. The controller is intentionally tunable and defaults to conservative constants to avoid surprises. - runtime/kv/priming_hysteresis.{cc,h} adds a short-lived (configurable 100-250ms) hysteresis token when a shard is primed; repeated priming for the same shard within the window is ignored to prevent thrash. - kernel/selector adjustments route lower-priority prefill kernels to background lanes when DLS signals low headroom; these use slower but memory-cheaper kernels (quantized paths) to keep throughput at cost-effective latency. - scheduler admission flow updated to consult POD multiplier before enlarging chunk sizes; continuous-batcher respects the damped target. - integration tests, microbenchmarks (tests/bench/prefill_wave_bench.py), and a perf doc (docs/perf/prefill-oscillation.md) were added. Performance summary: - End-to-end tail latency (p99) on our prefill-heavy chat workload reduced by 18-26% in stressed scenarios (high concurrency + KV churn). - Average throughput impact within 2-3% of baseline; in some high-churn tests throughput improved due to fewer wasted priming kernels. - KV prime churn reduced by ~35% in synthetic shard-scan tests. Safety and rollout: - Feature guarded by runtime flag redwood.prefill.pod.enabled (false by default). - Config maps for production tuned values placed under examples/experiments/prefill_smoother.yaml. - Gradual rollout plan: enable in Canary pool, monitor prefilling_kv_churn, decode_latency_p95, and scheduler_scale_events for 48h before broad rollout. Checklist: - [x] Implementation (pod controller, priming hysteresis, kernel routing) - [x] Unit tests for controller invariants and hysteresis window - [x] Integration benchmarks and manual validation on canary - [x] Docs and release notes - [x] Backwards compatible config flags and safe defaults Related: ENG-1325 (scheduling stability), ENG-1340 (kv priming regression triage), SUP-884 incident that motivated stronger hysteresis.

Arjun Mehta: Yes — added example config and validation in runtime/config.cc, default values kept conservative.

Arjun Mehta: Fixed in e5f1023 — switched to a lock-protected fast-path and optimized hot-path with epoch counters to avoid contention.
Priya Singh: Can we add a quick experiment to the perf dashboard to show before/after KV churn for canary?

ci_checks: benchmarks: perf/variant/prefill_wave: show 18-26% p99 reduction in stressed profile
release_notes: Introduce Prefill Oscillation Damper (POD) and Decode Latency Stabilizer (DLS): reduces prefill-induced tail latency by damping rapid prefill expansion and adding KV priming hysteresis. Feature behind runtime flag with conservative defaults. See docs/perf/prefill-oscillation.md for rollout guidance and tuning knobs.
notes_for_oncall: If enabling POD in a new pool, watch metrics: decode_latency_p95, scheduler_prefill_window_size, kv_prime_events, and prefill_background_kernel_ratio. If tail latency regresses, rollback by setting redwood.prefill.pod.enabled=false and revert the canary config.
testing: Unit tests added for controller math and hysteresis; integration bench compares baseline vs POD under KV-churn scenarios; manual canary verification performed for 48h before merge.
implementation_risks: Low/medium: new controller touches scheduler and kv priming fast paths; conservative defaults and feature flag minimize blast radius. The main risk observed during CI was a priming map race which was fixed. Additional risk: mis-tuned constants could reduce throughput under low-churn workloads; mitigated by conservative defaults and per-pool tunables.
rollout_plan: 0) Merge behind feature flag. 1) Enable in Canary (5% of traffic) for 48h. 2) If metrics stable, bump to 25% for 24h. 3) Full rollout. Alerts: prefilling_kv_churn > baseline*1.5 or decode_latency_p95 increased -> auto-disable in that pool.
user_impact: Transparent to API users. May reduce tail latency for chat workloads under high prefill churn. No changes to public API or config names; only internal runtime flags introduced.
notes: This PR focuses on behavior stability rather than raw throughput wins; the goal is to remove small oscillatory regressions that impacted customer p99 in production incidents. Future work: adaptive learning of controller constants and cross-GPU coordination of priming hysteresis.
